fixed-panel.note: the MX104 front photograph on the checked scale (#901): x = (px - 74.5) / 3.090 over the 437.0 mm body, y = (px - 8.5) / 3.067 down the 154.7 mm height (the issue's 3.061 is the same reading from a different edge pixel). The panel's lower edge meets the upper MIC plates at y 42.4. ALARM DB-15 shell 36.0-55.4 x 21.6-32.4. The four XE SFP+ cages are DISCRETE cages on a 17.2 mm pitch, each in its own bezel, not a ganged row: centres 98.0, 115.3, 132.4, 149.5 at y 28.2 (bezels 90.4-157.1 by 22.9-33.5), legends 2/0/0-2/0/3 above each and XE over a bracket at 123.8, so they are std/sfp, not std/sfp-ganged. ONLINE/OFFLINE button at (166.8, 30.0) with its legend under it, SYS OK lamp at (176.5, 24.6) under its legend. EXT REF CLOCK and TOD RJ45s centred at 271.0 and 286.9, y 12.3. The 1PPS and 10 MHz SMBs at 307.8, 315.7, 323.9, 331.7, y 13.2. Until 5.0.0 the cages were ganged at 14.25 from 97.8 (the last 8.9 mm left of the photograph's) at y 25.2, and the button and lamp sat about 11 and 20 mm left of where the photograph puts them. NOT DRAWN, and seen at the panel's right end: an ESD jack at about (379, 5) and a two-hole plate at about (406-422, 5) - follow-ups, not part of this re-placement

ground-stud-pitch.note: the hardware guide, grounding points specifications: 0.625-in. (15.86-mm) centres, which is 5/8 in., 15.875; the guide rounds the conversion. `ground-studs` is one placement of juniper/mx-ground-stud-pair-5-8@1, which composes juniper/mx-ground-stud@1 twice at exactly 15.875 (L116) and presents `stud-pair-5-8`, so one two-hole lug (generic/two-hole-lug-5-8@1) lands across the pair and the ring lug still lands on either stud, `ground-studs/1` and `/2`. The two studs were drawn 16.0 apart; they moved symmetrically about the midpoint the photograph placed, (205.0, 136.0), side by side, so a lug's wire leaves to the right, and their cutouts with them.

ground-stud-size.note: the hardware guide, grounding points specifications: two threaded holes that fit SAE 10-32 screws, spaced at 0.625 in. (15.86 mm) centres, for one two-hole cable lug: the `stud-size` of both studs.

lifecycle.note: announced - MX104 is EOL (TSB seen in the family tables; image-library page redirects). Per-SKU dates on the Juniper milestones page

mic-bays.note: the four MIC bays are the MIC plate, 168.8 x 29.2 (#261), placed off the front photograph. Across, at 3.090 px/mm (body 74.5 to 1425.0 px over 437.0 mm, confirmed by the ganged-SFP pitch at 3.091): the left plates start at 129.0 to 129.5 px, 17.8 mm, and the right at 652.5 px, 187.1 mm, a pitch of 523 px or 169.3 mm, which leaves a 0.5 mm seam between 168.8 plates. Down, on the chassis-height scale (473.5 px over 154.7 mm, 3.061, the top at 9.0 px): the upper plates run 138.75 to 229.5 px (42.4 to 72.0) and the lower 235.5 to 325.5 px (74.0 to 103.4), and a 29.2 plate centred in each gives y 42.6 and 74.1. The slot legends sit beside the plates' upper thirds, as printed. Until 4.0.0 the bays were 168 x 27 at x 17.8 and 193.0, y 49 and 81 - a 175.2 pitch and rows 6 to 7 mm low. The rest of the front's vertical frame is not re-measured here: the fixed XE row centre reads 28.3 against a modelled 25.2, and the PEM/RE band starts at 105.2 against 108.7.

other-faces.note: left face carries the estimated fan-tray band (side-mounted cooling per the guide); other faces rail-band estimates. Axis conventions per viewer3d.js as the siblings

pem-re-band.note: the MX104 front photograph on the scale above (#901). The band starts at y 105.5 (the issue read 105.2). The supply plates run x 7.0-113.8 and 114.7-221.5, y 105.5-153.7; the 103.7 x 45.0 supply contract is centred on each (pem0 at 8.55, pem1 at 116.25, y 107.1), which leaves the contract about 3 mm smaller than the photographed plate each way - a matter for juniper/mx104-psu-dc, not the bays. The Routing Engines run x 222.2-363.9 (141.7 against the 145.0 contract, centred at 220.55), RE1 from y 105.6 and RE0 from 129.0, RE legends at x 366.5 beside them; the plain side cover takes the rest of the right end, x 365.5-437.0 from the fixed panel down. Until 5.0.0 pem1 sat 8 mm right of its plate, both REs 36 mm right of theirs (over the side cover), and the band started at 108.7.

populated-with.note: photo - slot 1/0 and 0/1 carry MIC-3D-20GE-SFP, slot 1/1 the MIC-3D-4CHOC3-1OC12-CE, slot 0/0 the MIC-3D-2XGE-XFP; both RE bays carry the slim MX104 RE and both PSU bays the DC supply. Defaults reproduce that configuration

power.note: guide power consumption topic, Table 6 - 600 W for the AC router and 625 W for the DC router, measured from the power source (INPUT side) on a system with redundant supplies, redundant Routing Engines and the fan tray, fully loaded with MICs; 325 W AC and 350 W DC without MICs. The guide labels all four rows typical; the MX104 datasheet labels the loaded pair fully loaded (max) and the no-MIC pair typical. Carried as power-max-ac-w and power-max-dc-w with that disagreement in power-max-scope; the no-MIC rows stay here and are not carried. The guide has no per-module power table: the MIC and supply contracts carry their own figures, and the Routing Engine has none (see gaps)

rear.note: photo - a plain panel with the two-hole earthing plate at the bottom centre; nothing else. The fan tray and air filter are SIDE-mounted per the guide (Figure 7/8) and appear on the left face as an estimated band

scale.note: photo - the front photograph is isotropic, 3.090 px/mm across (body px 74.5-1425.0) and 3.067 down (px 8.5-483.0), cross-checked on the ganged-SFP pitch (#261, #901). Rows: fixed panel 0-42.4, the MIC rows (mic-bays), and the PSU/RE band from 105.5 (pem-re-band). A FIRST READING put the RE rows at 13.9 mm - too thin to hold their photographed RJ45s - and the row boundary was re-derived; positions are single-pass and approximate to ~2 mm throughout

sources.note: MX104 Hardware Guide, the MX104 datasheet, and the image-library photographs mx104-front-high and mx104-rear-high. No mechanical drawing was available
